title: Replace expired image refs with placeholder Markdown
description:
## Outcome

When an image file is gone, the stored Markdown no longer points at it. The source becomes a sentence anyone can read: `*[Removed image: sketch.png]*`. Download .md from the Share Link matches what readers see. Dead refs do not occupy the six image slots. Instant files the author edited out of the Markdown are deleted on Save, not left to bill the gigabyte until the 7-day clock.

## Why this slice

Deleting the file (previous child) reclaims storage. Leaving `![sketch.png](markshare-image:dead-id)` in the Document is a worse download, and it can block new pastes if the cap still counts refs. Local editor drafts can also resurrect a ref after cron deleted the file. Save has to sweep.

## Work

- Daily cleanup, after it deletes a due file, rewrites that Document's Markdown: each matching `markshare-image:` ref becomes `*[Removed image: {alt}]*`. Empty alt becomes `image`. Preserve surrounding Markdown. Do not rewrite unrelated images that are still live.
- Save does the same rewrite for any ref whose file is already gone, then persists that Markdown. If the author still has a local draft with the old ref, the next successful Save is what aligns source with storage.
- Save also deletes Instant files owned by this Document whose ids are no longer referenced in the Markdown being saved. That is the leftover-blob hole: paste, save, delete the line, save again, file gone.
- The six-image cap and the footer count live files plus pending referenced pastes. Placeholder lines and dead refs do not count. After rewrite, the author can paste again up to six live pictures.
- Download .md uses the stored Markdown. After cleanup rewrite, a reader who never opens the editor downloads the placeholder sentence.
- Lifecycle tests: due cleanup rewrites source and leaves live refs alone; Save with a dead ref persists the placeholder and does not re-upload; Save that drops a ref deletes that Instant file; counting ignores placeholders. Markdown tests: the placeholder sentence renders as text, not an image.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 7-day rule or the reader placeholder visual (previous child already defined both).
- Compressing images.
- A second cleanup schedule.

## Blocked by

- Expire stored images after 7 days and keep the Document (needs due-file deletion and the placeholder meaning).
- Concentrate pasted-image lifetime (markshare-6yx). Do not grow a second owner for "which images belong to this Document."
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- The placeholder Markdown form is settled: emphasis, not a new URL scheme, not an HTML comment. `*[Removed image: sketch.png]*` round-trips through any Markdown renderer and through Download .md.
- Rewrite is a Document lifecycle operation, not a string replace in App. It runs from cleanup (admin/removal path) and from Save (edit capability path).
- Only refs whose files are gone, or whose ids are being deleted in this pass, are rewritten. A Document with one live picture and one due picture keeps the live `markshare-image:` ref.
- Alt text comes from the Markdown image alt. That is usually the original filename. Do not fetch Instant metadata to name the placeholder.
- Count and footer: live Instant files still referenced, plus pending Files still referenced and not yet stored. markshare-6yx already requires the footer to match what Save will upload. This bead extends that fact to "live stored + pending", excluding placeholders and dead refs.
- Unreferenced Instant files are deleted on Save even if they have not hit 7 days. The author removed them from the Document. Keeping the bytes would defeat the allowances.
- Cleanup rewrite can race an open editor. That is accepted. The file stays gone. The next Save rewrites again if the draft still has the dead ref. Do not try to merge the editor's unsaved buffer from cron.
- Do not put Instant file URLs into Markdown. The private `markshare-image:` scheme remains the only in-source image form while the file lives.
- Tests at the lifecycle seam cover rewrite, slot reclaim, and unreferenced delete with the memory persistence/removal adapters. Do not add a third adapter. Markdown interpretation tests cover rendering the emphasis form as text.
- If markshare-6yx has not actually concentrated lifetime yet, stop and wait. Do not duplicate that module in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
Cleanup that deletes a due image rewrites that ref in stored Markdown to *[Removed image: {alt}]* and leaves live image refs untouched.
Download .md from the Share Link then contains the placeholder sentence, not a dead markshare-image ref.
Save replaces dead refs the same way, deletes Instant files no longer referenced in the Markdown, and does not count placeholders toward the six-image cap.
An author can paste a new image after expired ones have been rewritten.
Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Tighten pasted-image allowances to 2 MB and 6
description:
## Outcome

Authors can still paste a screenshot into a Document. They cannot paste a 5 MB original or a twentieth picture. The cap is 2 MB each, six per Document.

This is the burst control. It does not expire files. It stops one illustrated note from eating 100 MB of the Instant gigabyte.

## Current behaviour

Paste and drop accept PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF up to 5 MB, twenty per Document. The footer shows `n/20 images`. Oversized pastes explain "Each image must be 5 MB or smaller." Privacy copy repeats those numbers. Save also enforces the same limits against already-stored files plus new uploads.

## Work

- Change the named allowances to 2 MB and 6. Every check, footer, dialog, and public-information sentence must read from those names. Do not leave a hard-coded 5 MB or twenty in copy or tests.
- Reject a 2 MB + 1 byte paste and a seventh image the same way oversized and twenty-first images are rejected today: attach fails, Save fails, the Document is not published with the extra file.
- Keep type policy as it is. Do not add SVG, PDF, or video.
- Update Privacy (and any About / Acceptable use line that states the old numbers) so the published story matches the new caps. Image lifetime copy belongs to the expiry child, not this one.

## Out of scope

- Image TTL, placeholders, cleanup, or Markdown rewrite.
- Compressing on paste to squeeze under 2 MB.
- Changing Document expiry.

## Blocked by

None. Can start immediately.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Keep the limits in one named place on the image/Document-image policy. Footer, attach, Save, and public copy consume those names. A test that still says 5 MB or 20 is a miss.
- Attach and Save remain the two enforcement points. Attach catches paste/drop. Save catches a client that skipped attach, and counts already-stored images plus new uploads.
- The sixth image at exactly 2 MB still attaches. One byte over, or a seventh, does not.
- Error copy stays short and specific: each image must be 2 MB or smaller; a Document can include up to 6 images.
- markshare-6yx talks about an `n/20` footer matching the Save upload list. After this bead, that footer is `n/6`. Use the named maximum, not a new literal.
- Do not invent a second limit module. This is a policy change on the existing image attach/lifecycle path.
- Tests cover attach and Save at the lifecycle seam, plus the editor dialog copy, plus the public-information sentence. Replace old 5 MB / 20 assertions. Do not layer a parallel suite.
acceptance_criteria:
Pasting or dropping a file larger than 2 MB is rejected and explains that each image must be 2 MB or smaller.
A seventh image is rejected and explains that a Document can include up to 6 images.
A 2 MB file and a sixth image still attach and can be saved.
Footer, editor errors, lifecycle checks, and Privacy copy all use 2 MB and 6, with no leftover 5 MB or twenty.
Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Expire stored images after 7 days and keep the document
description: ## Outcome A stored pasted image lasts 7 days from upload. After that the Instant file is gone. The Document and its Share Link stay up. Where the picture was, Preview and the Reader show a designed text placeholder that uses the alt, usually the filename. Document expiry stays the optional clock it already is. Pictures are a second clock. Adding a screenshot does not make the note vanish. ## Why this slice Allowances bound a single Save. They do not stop months of leftover screenshots. Instant has no per-file TTL. MarkShare has to record the deadline, delete due files on the daily cron, and render something other than a broken image. The renderer already turns a `markshare-image:` ref with no source into the alt as a bare span. That is not good enough. The placeholder has to read as an intended removal, not a failed load. ## Work - On upload, record that this file is due 7 days later. Use one named 7-day policy. No author picker. - Daily cleanup deletes Instant files whose image deadline has been reached, including on Documents that are still available. It must not delete those Documents. The existing expired/deleted Document path still removes the Document and any leftover images. - After the file is gone, `imageSources` no longer includes that id. Markdown interpretation shows the designed placeholder in Preview and on the Share Link. Same module, both surfaces. - Files already in Instant without an image deadline get 7 days from rollout on the first cleanup pass (or an equivalent backfill). They then follow the same delete path. Do not delete them immediately. Do not leave them with no deadline. - Tell the author, briefly, that pictures are kept for 7 days. Share dialog and/or status footer is enough. Do not add a date picker for image lifetime. Update Privacy (and Acceptable use if it still implies pictures last as long as the Document) so the public story matches: Markdown can last until delete or Document expiry; pasted images last 7 days and then become placeholder text. - Injected-clock tests at the lifecycle seam: a file due in the future survives cleanup; at the exact deadline it is removed and the Document remains available. Markdown tests: a ref with no live source renders the placeholder, not an ``. ## Out of scope - Rewriting stored Markdown to `*[Removed image: …]*`. That is the next child. This slice may leave `markshare-image:` refs in the source while the file is gone. The reader still sees the placeholder because there is no live source. - Reclaiming the six image slots by stripping dead refs. Next child. - Deleting unreferenced Instant files on Save when the author edits the ref out. Next child, and related to markshare-6yx. - Changing optional Document expiry. ## Blocked by None. Can start in parallel with the allowances child.
design: ## Authoritative implementation contract - Seven days is a platform rule measured from upload time. Store it on the file (a custom `$files` field is allowed) or as an equivalent per-image fact the cleanup query can filter. Do not overload Document `expiresAt`. That field remains the whole-Document clock. - Cleanup lists due images independently of Document unavailability. A live Document can lose pictures and stay live. An unavailable Document still loses its pictures when the existing complete-deletion path runs. - Reader availability still depends only on missing / expired / deleted Document. Missing images are not Document unavailable. - Markdown interpretation owns the placeholder. When a `markshare-image:` ref has no displayable source, render a quiet, visible stand-in that includes the alt: Removed image: sketch.png. Do not use a broken ``. Do not invent a second renderer in App. - Preview and Share Link must match. A placeholder that exists only in the Reader is incomplete. - Existing files with no deadline: first cleanup (or backfill) sets deadline = now + 7 days, then they are ordinary due files on later passes. Use the injected clock. Do not depend on Instant `serverCreatedAt` for rollout grace; that would expire old production screenshots immediately. - Author-facing copy is factual and short. Example shape: Pictures are kept for 7 days. After that the document stays, with a placeholder where the picture was. Keep it off the Reader except as the placeholder itself. Share Link recipients should not see a countdown chrome. - Public-information pages are part of this slice because the behaviour changes the day files start disappearing. Caps copy may already say 2 MB / 6 if the allowances child landed; if not, do not revert those numbers, and do not block on that child. - Persistence and cleanup stay behind the Document lifecycle and removal seams. UI does not call Instant Storage. Cron remains the daily Vercel job. Extend outcomes so tests can see imagesRemoved on still-available Documents, not only Documents deleted. - Tests must not wait 7 real days. Jump the injected clock to the exact deadline, one millisecond before, and one millisecond after. - Do not weaken `$files` view rules to make expiry easier.
acceptance_criteria:
A stored image is deleted at 7 days from upload; the Document remains available on its Share Link.
Preview and Reader show a designed "Removed image: {alt}" placeholder instead of a broken image or Document unavailable.
Existing Instant files without a deadline receive 7 days from rollout and then follow the same path.
Optional Document expiry is unchanged.
Authors and Privacy copy state that pictures last 7 days and the writing stays.
Cleanup tests use an injected clock at the exact deadline.
Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Bound Instant storage for pasted images
description:
## Problem

MarkShare stores pasted images in Instant Storage. Instant's free tier is 1 GB of database space, and file storage counts toward that gigabyte. Today a Document can hold twenty images of 5 MB each: 100 MB in one note. Documents never expire unless the author sets a date. Images therefore live forever.

Ten fully loaded Documents fill the app. After that, everyone's Save starts failing. There are no accounts, so there is no per-person quota. Time and smaller allowances are the levers we actually have.

## Product outcome

Pasted images are cheap enough to offer and bounded enough not to sink the app.

- Each image is at most 2 MB. A Document holds at most six.
- Every stored image is deleted 7 days after upload. The Document stays. The Share Link stays.
- Where the picture was, readers see a designed text placeholder. The writing outlives the screenshot.
- Document expiry remains optional and separate. Adding a picture does not doom the note.

## Why not expire the whole Document

The first idea was to force a 1 / 7 / 30 day Document expiry whenever images were stored. That reclaims space, but it kills the Share Link because someone pasted a screenshot. MarkShare is a share link for writing, not a photo host. Keep the Markdown. Kill the bytes.

## Delivery slices

1. Tighten pasted-image allowances to 2 MB and 6.
2. Expire stored images after 7 days and keep the Document. Delete the Instant files. Show a designed placeholder. Backfill existing images. Tell authors and the public pages.
3. Replace expired image refs in stored Markdown with placeholder text, reclaim the six slots, and drop Instant files the Markdown no longer references.

## Success criteria

- A new paste larger than 2 MB, or a seventh image, is rejected with clear copy.
- An illustrated Document remains readable after its pictures are deleted. Readers see the placeholder, not a broken image and not Document unavailable.
- Daily cleanup deletes due image files without deleting a Document that is not itself expired or deleted.
- After rewrite, Download .md contains the placeholder sentence instead of a dead `markshare-image:` ref.
- Existing illustrated Documents enter the 7-day rule. They do not occupy Instant storage forever.
- Optional Document expiry is unchanged: never by default, whole Document unavailable at the chosen instant.

## Out of scope

- Compressing or resizing on paste.
- A picker for image lifetime. Seven days is a platform rule, not an author control.
- Per-user quotas, Instant Pro, or a global remaining-bytes check.
- Forcing Document expiry because images are present.
- Mermaid diagrams. They are text.

## Notes

Coordination bead only. Implement through the child beads in dependency order. Do not treat this epic as a coding slice.
design: ## Authoritative product rules These rules are settled. Child beads implement them. They do not reopen them. ### Allowances - Maximum image size is 2 MB. - Maximum images per Document is 6. - Supported types stay PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF. - The footer count and the Save upload list are the same fact: live stored files still referenced in Markdown, plus pending pastes still referenced and not yet stored. Dead refs and leftover Files do not count. ### Two clocks - Document `expiresAt` stays optional. Default remains never. At that instant the Share Link and Edit Link become the generic unavailable page. Daily cleanup then removes the Document and any remaining images. That path does not change. - Each stored image has its own expiry, 7 days from upload. When that instant is reached, the file is deleted. The Document remains available. ### Placeholder - The reader-facing stand-in uses the image alt, usually the filename: Removed image: sketch.png. - Stored Markdown, after rewrite, uses emphasis so any Markdown renderer can read it: `*[Removed image: sketch.png]*`. If alt is empty, use `image`. - The renderer must not show a broken `` for a `markshare-image:` ref with no live file. The designed placeholder is the intended state, not a fallback accident. - Preview and Share Link use the same interpretation path. The placeholder is not a second image policy in App. ### Rewrite timing - Daily cleanup deletes due Instant files and rewrites those refs in stored Markdown to the placeholder. That keeps Download .md honest for readers who never open the editor. - The author's next Save also replaces any `markshare-image:` ref that has no backing file, and deletes Instant files the Markdown no longer references. Local drafts can race the cron. Save-time sweep keeps the six slots honest. - Cleanup must not treat the editor as gospel. File gone is the source of truth. Markdown rewrite is how the Document records that. ### Existing images - Files already in Instant without an image expiry get 7 days from rollout, not 7 days from their original upload, and not immediate deletion. - First cleanup pass (or an equivalent backfill) writes that deadline so they enter the same delete-and-placeholder path. ### Architecture - Document lifecycle owns image allowances, upload-time expiry, due-file deletion, Markdown rewrite, and unreferenced-file removal. UI does not talk to Instant Storage. - Markdown interpretation owns rendering the placeholder. Capability-resolved `imageSources` remain the only way a real picture appears. - Scheduled cleanup stays on the existing daily cron. Extend it to due images on still-available Documents. Do not add a second sweeper. - Instant `$files` may grow a custom expiry field. Path layout `documents/{documentId}/{imageId}` stays. Share Links stay capability-gated. Do not open Storage view to the world. - Tests use the lifecycle and Markdown interpretation seams with an injected clock. Do not sleep on wall-clock 7 days. Do not assert Instant DSL in UI tests.
acceptance_criteria:
A Document with pictures stays readable after those pictures hit 7 days; the files are gone from Instant and readers see the placeholder.
New pastes are capped at 2 MB and 6 images per Document.
Optional Document expiry still defaults to never and still takes the whole link down at that instant.
Existing illustrated Documents receive a 7-day image deadline from rollout.
Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
notes: Coordination bead only. Implement through child beads in dependency order; do not treat the epic itself as a coding slice.

title: Deepen the Editor workspace
description:
## Why

`useEditorSession` already hides recovery, save, and pending blobs. App still has to learn the insides: remote `useEditDocument`, about 29 returned fields, Cmd+S, paste MIME, first-save `/new` replace, share/rotate/delete stacking, toasts, and five identical error overlays.

The session implementation is deep. The caller interface is not. Home, Editor, Reader, theme, and history dual-write all live in `App.tsx`.

## What to build

Deepen the Editor workspace. App should only route `editId` in and navigate. Share dialog, paste/drop, Cmd+S, first-save path replace, toasts, and error overlays sit behind that workspace interface. Keep `useEditorSession` as an internal seam, not a second public module.

## Scope limits

Do not extract five dialog modules or a toast module first. Those interfaces would be as large as their implementations. Do not reopen Document lifecycle or Markdown interpretation. Do not invent a clipboard module for copy-link work; that stays markshare-81p inside the share dialog.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- The Editor workspace module owns authoring chrome: session, share/rotate/delete dialogs, paste/drop, Cmd+S, first-save Edit Link replace, toasts, and split.
- App leftover knowledge is route kind, `editId`, navigate/replace, and theme. It must not still know pending images, recovery keys, dialog stacking, paste MIME, or `publishedEditId !== editId` loading.
- `useEditorSession` and `useEditorSplit` stay internal. Do not extract `persistRecovery`, `insertSnippet`, or access helpers into new files.
- DocumentLifecycle remains an injected adapter at the existing seam. The workspace must not import the raw Instant client.
- Absorb `formatExpiry` / `toDatetimeLocalValue` into the workspace and Reader presentation. Do not grow `document.ts` into a dates module.
- Browser dependencies are local-substitutable. Tests drive workspace outcomes: save, share open, paste, failure dialogs, first-save path replace. Do not keep proving session behaviour only by rendering the whole App shell with a fake lifecycle.
- Copy Share/Edit Links (markshare-81p) belongs in the share dialog once that work lands. Do not create a separate clipboard module here.
acceptance_criteria:
- App routes editId into the Editor workspace and navigates; it no longer owns share dialog stacking, Cmd+S, paste MIME, first-save path replace, toasts, or error overlays.
- useEditorSession remains an internal seam, not a second public module with a 29-field caller interface.
- DocumentLifecycle stays injected; the workspace does not import the Instant client.
- Workspace tests cover save, share open, paste, failure dialogs, and first-save Edit Link replace through the workspace interface.
- Isolated dialog or toast modules are not extracted as public interfaces.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
notes:
Architecture review 16 Aug — new evidence, scope unchanged.

Three fixes landed 15–16 Aug inside the exact code this deepening absorbs: b8aeeed (copy Share and Edit Links), 5803295 (keep ordinary toasts under the dialog, newest copy speaks), 27a15d0 (confirmation follows the clipboard, not the click). App.tsx is the most-changed file on the branch.

Measured on 560e294: useEditorSession returns 27 keys, 13 of them feedback plumbing — 5 error strings, 2 notice flags, 6 dismiss functions. App renders 5 near-identical error overlays, owns a third 1900 ms timer for the copy notice, and expresses toast precedence as an inline '!copyNotice &&' guard in JSX.

The existing scope limit still holds: absorb this into the workspace interface rather than extracting dialog or toast modules whose interfaces would match their implementations.

title: Concentrate pasted-image lifetime
description:
## Why

A pasted image is one product fact with six owners. The Editor session keeps the File. Save uploads every unuploaded pending image, even after the Markdown ref is gone. Instant Storage does the PUT. The edit query later supplies `imageSources`. Markdown renders those sources. App tests mock the lifecycle and never send `images`.

That scatter is already in production: leftover pending Files still go on Save, the footer `n/20` can disagree with what Save uploads, and the suite stays green because the mock skips uploads.

## What to build

Concentrate pasted-image lifetime behind one module interface. Attach, drop-when-unref'd, the footer count, and what Save actually uploads must be the same fact. Blob preview URLs stay session implementation. Instant Storage stays behind the existing persistence adapter.

## Scope limits

Do not reopen Instant `$files.create` permissions. That is markshare-iyw. Do not add a `pending-images` module. Do not put Instant file URLs into Markdown source. Do not add a second Instant client in App.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- One module owns which images belong to the current Document: refs still in Markdown, the `n/20` count, and the list Save will upload.
- Blob preview URLs and `URL.revokeObjectURL` stay inside the Editor session implementation. They are not part of the lifecycle interface.
- Instant Storage upload, path layout, and `$files` rules stay behind the existing Document persistence adapter. UI modules must not call Instant Storage.
- Save must not upload a pending File whose id is gone from the Markdown. The footer count must match that list.
- The module interface is the test surface. Cover leftover-after-delete, save-time upload of referenced images only, and a denied persistence create that fails Save without publishing a Document.
- Replace the App-test mock that rebuilds `imageSources` from Markdown and ignores `images` on save. Use the existing memory persistence adapter. Do not layer a third adapter.
- Keep Markdown interpretation as the render-safety seam. Capability-resolved `imageSources` remain the only way an image appears.
acceptance_criteria:
- Save uploads only images still referenced in the Markdown; leftover pending Files after a deleted ref are not sent.
- The footer n/20 count matches what Save will actually upload.
- Blob preview URLs stay inside the Editor session implementation; UI modules do not call Instant Storage.
- Tests at the module interface cover leftover-after-delete, referenced-only upload, and a denied persistence create that fails Save without publishing.
- App tests no longer mock documentLifecycle with a skip-images adapter; they use the existing memory persistence adapter.
- Instant $files.create permission work stays in markshare-iyw.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Saving fails once a pasted image is in the editor session
description:
## Problem

On the deployed app (https://md-viewer-nine-teal.vercel.app), Save changes fails as soon as the editor session has a pasted image. The dialog is:

> Document not saved
> We could not save this document. Please try again.

Plain Markdown without a pasted image saves. A first save and a later revision both work. The failure is not "Markdown with an image in the source" in the abstract — it is Instant Storage rejecting the upload, and the editor then aborting the whole save.

That also explains the false lead. Deleting the `![...](markshare-image:…)` line, or replacing the document with test Markdown, still fails in the same session. The footer keeps showing `1/20 images`. Pending uploads are not dropped when the Markdown no longer references them, so Save still PUTs the file and Instant still denies it.

## Reproduction (production, 2026-08-14)

Confirmed against production, not mocks.

1. Create a document. Type `# Test markdown` with no image. Save. Succeeds. URL becomes `/e/…`, share URL `/s/…` is live, a new tab can read it.
2. Paste a 1×1 PNG into the same editor. Markdown gains `![pixel.png](markshare-image:…)`, footer becomes `1/20 images`.
3. Save. Dialog: Document not saved.
4. Instant response:

```
PUT https://api.instantdb.com/storage/upload
400
{"type":"permission-denied","message":"Permission denied: not has-storage-permission?","hint":{"input":["$files","create"],"expected":"has-storage-permission?"}}
```

5. Replace the editor contents with `# Test markdown` and no image ref. Footer still `1/20 images`. Save. Same 400. Same dialog.

Trace IDs from those two denied uploads: `8119bc411b485caa5216e89a6a7f67a1`, `9499182c7502d3e81e770e2d6a7f67bd`.

## Cause

`lifecycle.save` uploads pending images before it writes the document (`src/document-lifecycle.ts`, `src/lib/instant-document-persistence.ts`). `db.storage.uploadFile` is a PUT to Instant Storage. Instant evaluates `$files.allow.create`. That check is failing on the live app.

Repo rule today:

```
$files.allow.create: data.path.startsWith('documents/')
```

`$files` defaults to deny in Instant if the rule is missing or false. Two live possibilities, in this order:

1. The `$files` rules in `instant.perms.ts` were never pushed to the production Instant app after markshare-03o. Document create/update already worked, so an unpushed `$files` block would look exactly like this: text saves work, uploads 400.
2. The rules are live, but Instant Storage create does not see `data.path` the way the CEL expression expects, so `startsWith('documents/')` is false. Instant's own getting-started rule is `create: "true"`. `uploadFile` also cannot pass `ruleParams` in the current SDK, so create cannot be gated on `editId` the way view/delete are.

Do not guess past that. Confirm the live Instant permissions first (`npx instant-cli pull perms` or the dashboard). Then make `$files.create` allow `documents/{documentId}/{imageId}` uploads and push.

Secondary product bug, same save path: `pendingImages` in `useEditorSession` is only cleared when published `imageSources` arrive. Removing the Markdown ref does not drop the File. Until upload works, that session cannot save anything.

Errors are swallowed. `createDocumentLifecycle.save` catches and returns `{ kind: 'failed' }`. The editor always shows the generic sentence. Production evidence lives in the Instant 400, not the UI.

## Expected

- Pasting a supported image and saving publishes the document and the image.
- Replacing Markdown with text that has no image still saves, even if a paste happened earlier in the session (either because the leftover pending file is dropped, or because upload now succeeds and unreferenced files are not sent).
- A document that never had an image continues to save.
- Instant `$files` view stays capability-gated. Do not open Storage to the world to make create work.
- After changing perms: `npx instant-cli push perms --yes` against the production Instant app, then repeat the production paste-and-save.

## Out of scope

- markshare-bxw (Share Links opening as unavailable). A fresh `/s/:id` load of a text-only document worked during this investigation.
- Copy-to-clipboard (markshare-81p).
- Broader error-copy redesign, except do not keep swallowing the Instant 400 if a small persistence-level signal would prevent another silent save death.
design:
## Authoritative diagnosis and fix contract

Confirmed on production: Save dies in Instant Storage, not in Markdown parsing, title extraction, or document `transact`.

### 1. Prove which `$files.create` Instant is actually running

Pull live perms. Compare to `instant.perms.ts`.

- If `$files.create` is missing or still default-false, push the repo rules (after they are known-good) with `npx instant-cli push perms --yes`.
- If the repo rule is already live, it is evaluating false during `uploadFile`. Change the CEL so Instant Storage create allows paths under `documents/`. Instant documents `create: "true"` for uploads; path restriction via `data.path.startsWith(...)` is the documented pattern, but it is the thing failing here. Probe with the smallest rule that still keeps uploads inside `documents/`. Do not set view or delete to `"true"`.

`db.storage.uploadFile` does not take `ruleParams` in `@instantdb/react` 1.0.65. Do not invent an edit-capability check on create that the SDK cannot send.

### 2. Do not upload images the Markdown no longer references

Even after create is fixed, Save should not send leftover `pendingImages` whose ids are gone from the Markdown. Either drop those pending files when the ref is removed, or filter them out in `save`. The footer `n/20 images` must match what Save will actually upload.

### 3. Keep the failure at the persistence seam

UI must not call Instant Storage. Lifecycle already rolls back uploaded ids on failure; keep that. If the Instant 400 is still mapped to a generic failed save, add a test at `instant-document-persistence` / lifecycle that a denied `$files` create fails the save and does not leave a published document. Do not add a second Instant client in App.

### 4. Verify on the deployed app, not only Vitest

Mocks never hit `/storage/upload`. After perms are pushed:

1. New document, text only, save — still works.
2. Paste a tiny PNG, save — Changes saved, share link shows the image.
3. Paste, delete the Markdown ref, save — succeeds; no stray upload of the removed file.

title: Share Links open as Document unavailable in a new tab
description:
## Problem

A published Share Link is immediately treated as unavailable when a reader opens it. After the author selects the link or pastes it into a new tab, MarkShare shows:

> Document unavailable
> This share link is invalid or the document is no longer available.

That page is the correct generic response for unknown, expired, and deleted Documents. It is not correct for a Document that was just saved and whose Share Link is still live.

Sharing is the product. A live Share Link that cannot be opened is a broken publish path, not a privacy or expiry outcome.

## Reproduction

1. Create a Document and save it so it is live.
2. Open Share (or use the footer Share URL).
3. Select the read-only Share Link, or copy it and enter it in a new tab.
4. The Reader immediately shows Document unavailable instead of the published Markdown.

Also check the in-app "Open share link" toast path. Current tests mostly navigate inside the SPA; the reported failure is opening the URL as a fresh tab or by selecting/entering the link.

## Expected

Anyone with a live Share Link can read the saved Document. The same URL must keep working across:

- selecting or copying the URL from the Share dialog
- pasting or typing it into a new tab
- a full page load, not only in-app `pushState` navigation
- a browser that never authored the Document

The generic unavailable page remains only for unknown, malformed, expired, and deleted links, with no extra reason disclosed.

## Out of scope

- Copy-to-clipboard affordances (separate bead)
- Changing expiry, deletion, or privacy wording
- Edit Link restore or rotation behaviour, except where it is required to prove Share Links stay read-only and available
design:
## Authoritative diagnosis and fix contract

- Keep one Reader unavailable outcome. Do not add a distinct "just published but not found" page, error code, or reason that would distinguish missing, expired, deleted, or failed lookups.
- Treat a full document load of `/s/:id` as a first-class path. A fix that only works through in-app `onNavigate(sharePath(id))` is incomplete.
- Investigate at the real seams, in this order, and record which one actually fails:
  1. Route recognition and ID encoding (`sharePath` / `recognizeRoute` / `decodeURIComponent`) when the URL is copied, truncated in the link box, or loaded in a new tab.
  2. InstantDB share lookup: `useShareDocument` must query by document `id` and pass `ruleParams.knownDocumentId`. A missing or mismatched rule param yields the same unavailable page.
  3. Persistence vs SPA: confirm the Document exists for a fresh client that has no editor session, remembered edit capability, or prior IndexedDB state.
  4. Display vs copied URL: the Share dialog and footer truncate with ellipsis. Confirm whether users are opening a truncated token or the real ID.
- Do not weaken InstantDB view rules to "allow all" or return `editId` to Share Link holders. Share Links stay read-only; Edit Links stay private.
- Tests must cover a fresh Share Link load with only the opaque document ID, not only editor-session navigation after save. Include a case that would catch ID encoding and a case that would catch a missing `knownDocumentId` rule param.
- Replace overlapping incidental App tests once the lifecycle/navigation coverage exists; do not layer duplicate suites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Saving a Document produces a Share Link that opens the published Markdown for a visitor who never authored it.
- Selecting the Share Link, copying it, pasting it into a new tab, and loading `/s/:id` as a full page all show the Reader, not Document unavailable.
- Unknown, malformed, expired, and deleted Share Links still show the same generic unavailable page and never disclose content or Edit Link capability.
- Automated coverage proves a fresh share-ID load, not only in-app navigation from the editor after save.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #11: share URLs are full-value inputs so a new tab gets the real document ID.

title: Verify Mermaid readability across MarkShare surfaces
description:
## Outcome

The adaptive diagram experience is proven in the actual Editor Preview and published Share Link, not only in isolated component tests. Existing Mermaid safety and Markdown reading behaviour remain unchanged.

## Verification matrix

- Surfaces: desktop split Preview, mobile Preview tab, desktop Share Link, and mobile Share Link.
- Widths: 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420, and 320 pixels, including editor split changes at desktop widths.
- Themes: light and dark.
- Diagram shapes: a small diagram that fits, the representative eight-stage left-to-right flowchart, a much wider overflow case, a tall diagram, and samples from sequence, class, state, and ER syntax.
- Inputs: pointer, wheel, trackpad-style scrolling, keyboard-only use, and touch-size interaction.
- States: loading, successful render, invalid source fallback, source change, viewport resize, open viewer, close and reopen, and more than one diagram in a document.

## Work

- Add focused automated tests at the Mermaid component boundary for geometry, controls, state transitions, cleanup, and accessibility.
- Add integration coverage proving Preview and Share Link share the same component and adaptive policy.
- Retain hostile Mermaid tests for strict configuration, rejected interactive input, sanitization, and safe fallback.
- Perform and record browser checks for SVG readability, overflow cues, tooltip placement, focus order, gestures, overlay containment, and absence of page-level horizontal overflow.
- Confirm that non-diagram Markdown retains its existing text measures and rendering.
- Run the full repository verification suite.

## Out of scope

Do not weaken acceptance because jsdom lacks layout. Use controlled geometry fakes for deterministic component tests and real-browser checks for layout and gestures.
design:
## Authoritative verification contract

- Test product outcomes through the Mermaid presentation boundary and rendered surfaces. Avoid making CSS text matching the primary proof of adaptive behaviour.
- Stub ResizeObserver and SVG geometry explicitly in unit tests so fit, wide-lane, and overflow thresholds are deterministic.
- Use real Mermaid rendering in at least one browser verification path so sanitized SVG viewBox handling and internal IDs are exercised.
- Check keyboard focus containment and restoration with observable focus assertions. Check listener and body-state cleanup by closing and unmounting during active interactions.
- Treat Preview and Share Link parity as an invariant. A fix that exists on one surface only is incomplete.
- Preserve the existing Markdown safety test suite. Pan and zoom work must not broaden Mermaid input or output permissions.
- Record any gesture limitation that cannot be automated, with exact device or browser steps and observed result.
acceptance_criteria:
- The complete verification matrix has automated coverage or an explicit recorded browser result.
- The representative eight-stage flowchart no longer renders with approximately 5px labels; it uses the wider lane and readable horizontal overflow as designed.
- Fitting, wide, overflowing, tall, and multiple diagrams behave independently across Preview and Share Link.
- Expanded-view pointer, keyboard, wheel, trackpad, and touch behaviour is verified at supported viewport sizes.
- Light and dark themes, focus handling, tooltip access, reduced motion, resize, rerender, cleanup, and invalid fallback are verified.
- Non-diagram Markdown measure and existing strict Mermaid security outcomes do not regress.
- There is no page-level horizontal overflow at any supported width.
- npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run build all pass.
notes: Verified 2026-08-14: automated 42-test suite plus browser checks at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420, and 320px; representative flow, dark tokens, mobile overlay, single SVG, focus restoration, and no page overflow.

title: Build the accessible expanded Mermaid viewer
description:
## Outcome

A reader can open a wide Mermaid diagram in a near-full-screen MarkShare overlay, see the complete diagram first, and inspect detail with predictable pan and zoom controls on desktop, keyboard, trackpad, and touch devices.

## Work

- Open the viewer only from the diagram expand icon.
- Use almost the full viewport with a small desktop margin and an edge-to-edge mobile layout.
- Show one diagram at a time. Do not add previous or next navigation.
- Start every opening in Fit mode and reset to Fit when the viewer closes, reopens, or receives new diagram output.
- Provide visible Zoom in, Zoom out, and Fit controls. Use 400% as the initial maximum zoom and keep the limit in one named policy value.
- Support pointer drag to pan, mouse-wheel zoom, two-finger trackpad pan, pinch zoom, plus and minus zoom shortcuts, arrow-key panning, and 0 for Fit.
- Close through the visible close control, Escape, or the backdrop. A pointer action within the viewer must not trigger backdrop close.
- Trap focus while open, give the overlay a useful accessible name, prevent background interaction, and restore focus to the originating expand icon after close.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences and clean up document listeners, pointer capture, body state, and gesture state on close and unmount.

## Out of scope

Do not use the browser Fullscreen API. Do not add export, copy, minimap, diagram editing, or gallery navigation.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Build a reusable accessible overlay primitive suitable for this diagram viewer rather than stretching the current fixed 520px publish dialog styles. Shared low-level backdrop and focus behaviour may be factored without changing publish behaviour.
- Keep viewport transform state behind one interface with Fit, zoomBy, zoomTo, and panBy operations. Buttons, keyboard, pointer, wheel, and touch all call the same operations.
- Derive Fit from the current SVG viewBox and live viewer bounds. Recompute it on viewer resize and mobile orientation change without exceeding 100% natural scale unless the reader explicitly zooms in.
- Constrain zoom from Fit or the smallest useful scale through the named 400% maximum. Keep enough of the diagram reachable that panning cannot permanently lose it outside the viewport.
- Do not mount the same Mermaid SVG string twice with duplicate internal IDs. Either move or portal one live diagram presentation, or render a second SVG with a unique Mermaid render ID and valid internal references.
- If a zoom library is selected, declare it as a direct dependency and wrap it behind the viewer transform interface. Do not import Mermaid transitive d3-zoom by accident.
- Prevent wheel handling outside the open viewer and preserve expected two-finger trackpad panning. Use non-passive listeners only where preventDefault is required.
- Accessibility behaviour is part of correctness, not a later visual QA task.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting the inline expand icon opens one labelled near-full-screen viewer and places focus inside it.
- The diagram initially fits the viewer and resets to Fit after close, reopen, source change, and responsive resize.
- Visible buttons, plus and minus, 0, arrow keys, mouse wheel, pointer drag, two-finger trackpad pan, and pinch gestures operate through one bounded transform model.
- Zoom cannot exceed the named 400% initial maximum and the diagram cannot become permanently unreachable through panning.
- Close, Escape, and backdrop close work; interaction inside the viewer does not close it; focus returns to the originating icon.
- Background content cannot receive focus or scroll while the viewer is open, and all global listeners and body state are removed after close or unmount.
- No duplicate SVG IDs or broken marker, clip-path, or style references occur while the viewer is open.
- Automated interaction and accessibility tests pass with type checking, lint, and production build.
notes: Implemented accessible 400% expanded viewer with shared transform controls, focus containment/restoration, and cleanup.

title: Present Mermaid diagrams with clear inline controls and overflow cues
description:
## Outcome

Every valid Mermaid diagram has a consistent token-based panel. Readers can identify wide content, move through it without losing readability, and discover the expanded viewer without cluttering diagrams that already fit.

## Work

- Give every successfully rendered Mermaid diagram a subtle panel with theme-token background, border, radius, and padding.
- Centre diagrams that fit. Start horizontally overflowing diagrams at the left edge.
- Preserve native horizontal wheel, trackpad, touch, keyboard, and scrollbar access to inline overflow.
- When content exists beyond the visible right edge, show a soft edge fade and the short text Scroll to view.
- Remove the text after the reader first scrolls that diagram. Keep edge fades synchronized with the actual left and right overflow boundaries.
- Show an icon-only expand control only when the adaptive sizing policy marks the diagram as needing the wide treatment.
- Place the control at the top-right in a dedicated area that never covers the SVG.
- Give the icon an accessible name and a concise tooltip on pointer hover and keyboard focus. Do not depend on hover for the accessible name or touch operation.
- Reset hint dismissal, overflow cues, and inline scroll position when changed Markdown creates a new diagram.

## Out of scope

This bead does not implement expanded-view pan and zoom, export actions, previous or next diagram navigation, or author configuration.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Consume the sizing result from markshare-9df.1. Do not create a second width or readability heuristic in the control frame.
- Keep panel, cue, and expand-control state local to each diagram instance so documents with several diagrams do not affect one another.
- Calculate fades from real scrollWidth, clientWidth, and scrollLeft state, including fractional values and resize changes. Treat the native scrollbar as functional input, not decoration.
- Use existing MarkShare tokens and focus-visible conventions in both themes. Do not introduce hard-coded light-only colours.
- Keep loading and invalid Mermaid fallback behaviour distinct. The successful diagram panel must not conceal the existing safe source fallback.
- The expand icon announces the expanded-view action to assistive technology even when its visible tooltip is absent on touch devices.
acceptance_criteria:
- All successfully rendered diagrams use the subtle panel in Preview and Share Link, in light and dark themes.
- Fitting diagrams are centred and do not show overflow guidance or an expand control.
- Adaptive wide diagrams begin at the left, remain horizontally scrollable, show accurate overflow fades, and initially show Scroll to view.
- The text hint disappears after the first horizontal interaction for that diagram while boundary fades remain accurate.
- The expand icon appears only for diagrams that need wide treatment, does not cover SVG content, has an accessible name, and exposes its tooltip on hover and focus.
- New Mermaid output resets the inline position and cue state.
- Component tests cover multiple independent diagrams, scrolling to both boundaries, resize, source change, keyboard focus, tooltip behaviour, and both themes; type checking, lint, and build pass.
notes: Implemented token panel, native overflow cues, per-diagram hint reset, and wide-only accessible expand control.

title: Establish adaptive Mermaid sizing and the wide document lane
description:
## Outcome

The shared Mermaid component can distinguish a diagram that fits the prose measure from one that would become unreadable, and the document layout gives only that diagram access to a wider lane.

## Work

- Normalize sanitized Mermaid SVG dimensions from a valid viewBox after every render.
- Observe the diagram lane when it mounts and whenever the Preview split, Reader viewport, mobile tab, font metrics, or window size changes.
- Preserve natural SVG size when it fits. Scale down only as far as 0.875 of natural size. Use the wide lane when the prose column would require a smaller scale.
- If the wider lane is still smaller than 0.875 of the natural SVG width, keep the SVG at the readable minimum and allow overflow.
- Keep ordinary Markdown content at 62ch in Preview and 66ch in Reader while allowing an adaptive diagram frame to use the available pane or page width with the existing page padding.
- Reset derived size and scroll state when Mermaid renders a new SVG for changed source.
- Handle missing, zero, malformed, or changing SVG geometry without throwing or bypassing the existing safe fallback.

## Out of scope

Do not add the visual scroll hint, expand button, expanded viewer, export actions, author sizing directives, or source rewriting in this bead.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Keep one Mermaid rendering path under MarkdownView. A focused Mermaid presentation component can be extracted from markdown.tsx, but Markdown interpretation remains the owner of recognition and safety policy.
- Base adaptation on sanitized SVG geometry, not source parsing or flowchart-only Mermaid configuration. The same algorithm must work for flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, and other SVG-backed Mermaid types.
- Model natural size, available prose width, available wide-lane width, effective scale, and overflow as explicit derived state. Avoid one-off CSS aspect-ratio heuristics.
- Prefer ResizeObserver at the diagram boundary and make observer setup, stale callbacks, and teardown deterministic in tests.
- Do not widen the entire article. The rendered document needs a stable readable-content lane plus an intentional diagram breakout mechanism.
- Preserve SVG aspect ratio and sharp vector rendering. Do not set a fixed diagram height or rasterize the output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every rendered Mermaid SVG receives a valid natural-size and effective-scale decision from its viewBox.
- A diagram that fits remains in the readable content lane at natural size.
- A diagram that would fall below 0.875 scale uses the wider lane; if that lane is still insufficient, the SVG remains at 0.875 scale and overflows horizontally.
- Preview and Reader prose retain their 62ch and 66ch measures while adaptive diagrams use their available wider space.
- Resizing the editor split, viewport, or mobile layout recomputes the decision without stale state or leaked observers.
- Changed Mermaid source resets the sizing and scroll decision.
- Missing or malformed dimensions fail safely.
- Focused component tests cover fit, wide-lane, overflow, resize, rerender, and cleanup outcomes; type checking, lint, and build pass.
notes: Implemented adaptive viewBox sizing, 0.875 readable minimum, wide lane, resize/rerender cleanup tests.

title: Make Mermaid diagrams readable and explorable
description:
## Problem

Wide Mermaid diagrams are currently scaled to 100% of the narrow Markdown text measure. A representative eight-stage left-to-right flowchart has a 1804 by 62.5 SVG viewBox but renders at about 553 by 19 pixels in Preview. Its normal 16px labels become about 5px and cannot be read.

## Product outcome

Mermaid diagrams remain readable without making prose lines wider. Every diagram has a subtle container. A diagram that cannot fit the prose measure at a readable scale uses the wider document lane, preserves readable labels, and scrolls horizontally when needed. Wide diagrams can open in an accessible near-full-screen viewer with pan and zoom.

## Scope

- Apply one automatic policy to every Mermaid diagram type.
- Apply the same behaviour in Preview and the published Share Link on desktop and mobile.
- Keep prose at the existing 62ch Preview and 66ch Reader measures.
- Do not require author directives or silently rewrite diagram source.
- Do not add SVG or PNG export, diagram-gallery navigation, or browser Fullscreen API behaviour.
- Treat 400% as the initial maximum zoom and keep that policy easy to revise.

## Delivery slices

1. Establish adaptive Mermaid sizing and the wide document lane.
2. Add the common diagram container, overflow cues, and expand affordance.
3. Build the accessible expanded diagram viewer.
4. Verify the complete behaviour across routes, diagram types, themes, inputs, and responsive sizes.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the existing shared Markdown interpretation path. Preview and Reader must continue to render the same MarkdownView and one Mermaid security policy.
- Keep Mermaid initialization, strict input rejection, SVG sanitization, invalid-diagram fallback, sizing, and presentation behind one Mermaid diagram component boundary. Do not add a second renderer or duplicate policy in App.
- Determine presentation from the sanitized rendered SVG viewBox and the available container width. Do not parse Mermaid syntax, diagram direction, or diagram type to guess size.
- Preserve natural SVG size when it fits. A diagram may scale down only to an effective scale of 0.875, which maps Mermaid default 16px labels to about 14px. If the diagram still does not fit, widen its lane and then use horizontal overflow instead of further shrinking it.
- Keep Preview prose at 62ch and Reader prose at 66ch. Give only adaptive diagram frames access to the wider scroll container; do not widen headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code, or fallback source.
- Every successfully rendered diagram uses the same token-based panel. Diagrams that fit are centred. Overflowing diagrams start at the left edge.
- The expanded viewer must not mount duplicate copies of the same ID-bearing SVG. Reuse one live SVG presentation or render a separately identified SVG so marker, clip-path, and style references remain valid.
- If a pan or zoom package is used, add it as a direct dependency. Do not rely on Mermaid transitive dependencies.
- Treat focus management, keyboard interaction, pointer and touch input, reduced-motion preferences, theme parity, ResizeObserver behaviour, and cleanup as part of the component contract.
- Tests must observe component and user outcomes. CSS source-string checks alone do not prove this feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Mermaid diagram has the agreed subtle container in Preview and Share Link.
- Diagrams stay at natural scale when possible and never shrink below the agreed effective 0.875 scale; wider content gets a wide lane and horizontal scrolling.
- Only diagrams that need the adaptive wide treatment expose an expand icon and overflow guidance.
- The expanded viewer provides the agreed accessible pan, zoom, Fit, close, reset, pointer, touch, and keyboard behaviour.
- Existing strict Mermaid input policy, SVG sanitization, invalid fallback, prose measures, and Preview/Reader equivalence remain intact.
- Automated tests, type checking, lint, production build, and documented responsive browser checks pass.
notes:
Coordination bead only. Implement through child beads markshare-9df.1 to markshare-9df.4 in dependency order; do not treat the epic itself as a coding slice.
All four delivery slices completed and verified.

title: Deepen the Document lifecycle before Edit Links
description:
## Why

The Editor and Reader currently construct InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, timestamps, and failure meaning directly. The document test reproduces that third-party implementation with a Proxy. Edit Links, private images, expiry, and deletion would multiply this leakage.

## What to build

Deepen the Document lifecycle before adding Edit Links. Concentrate publication, reading, capability enforcement, timestamps, and lifecycle outcome translation in one module with a small interface. Put InstantDB behind the true external seam: an InstantDB adapter in production and an in-memory or mock adapter in tests.

Preserve the existing anonymous publish, Share Link, read-only Reader, and generic unavailable behaviour.

## Scope limits

Do not implement Edit Links, images, expiry, cleanup, or new product behaviour here. Do not introduce ports for dependencies that do not vary.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- The Document lifecycle module owns persistence orchestration and capability rules.
- UI modules must not import the raw InstantDB client or construct transaction/query DSL, ruleParams, IDs, or timestamps.
- InstantDB is the production adapter. Tests use a second adapter, making this a real seam.
- Translate third-party loading, missing, and failure states into domain outcomes inside the module.
- The module interface is the test surface. Tests assert publish/read/unavailable outcomes and do not recreate InstantDB internals.
- Replace obsolete helper-level or DSL-mock tests once equivalent interface tests exist; do not layer both suites.
- Keep route grammar and Markdown interpretation outside this module.
acceptance_criteria:
- Editor and Reader no longer construct InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, IDs, or timestamps.
- One production InstantDB adapter and one in-memory or mock test adapter satisfy the Document lifecycle seam.
- Existing publish, Share Link, read-only Reader, and generic unavailable behaviour remain unchanged.
- Tests exercise lifecycle outcomes through the module interface without reproducing the InstantDB transaction/query DSL.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Add expiry and complete deletion
description:
## What to build

Documents never expire by default. An editor can set a local date/time expiry; access stops exactly at that time; manual deletion and the daily Vercel cleanup remove Document and image records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Share Link returns the same unavailable response for a deleted or expired Document immediately after its expiry time.
- [ ] Expired and deleted Documents, including their pasted images, are removed by the cleanup process within 24 hours.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Support private pasted images.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the deep Document lifecycle module from markshare-ntg with expiry evaluation, deletion, and cleanup outcomes.
- Reader callers receive the same unavailable outcome for missing, expired, and deleted Documents; storage details and reason distinctions must not leak across the interface.
- Manual deletion and scheduled cleanup share lifecycle rules so Document and image removal cannot drift.
- Keep the Vercel schedule/transport at an internal seam with production and test adapters only where behaviour genuinely varies.
- Test expiry at exact timestamps with an injected clock or equivalent deterministic mechanism; do not rely on wall-clock sleeps.
- Test complete Document-plus-image deletion through lifecycle outcomes rather than InstantDB internals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documents never expire by default and become unavailable exactly at a configured expiry time.
- Missing, expired, and deleted Documents produce the same externally observable unavailable result.
- Manual deletion and scheduled cleanup remove the Document and all owned images within the agreed window.
- Expiry and cleanup tests are deterministic and exercise the Document lifecycle interface without wall-clock sleeps or raw InstantDB assertions.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6: document expiry, deletion, and scheduled cleanup.

title: Apply privacy, abuse, and public-information controls
description:
## What to build

MarkShare has no analytics or content logging; protects Share Links from search indexing and referrer leakage; gives private generic link previews; applies Vercel protection and rate limits; and publishes About, Privacy, and Acceptable Use pages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Share Links do not expose Document titles or content to search engines, link previews, referrers, analytics, or application logs.
- [ ] Public creation and image upload are rate-limited, and the public-information pages describe the agreed service behaviour.

## Blocked by

- Create and read a basic Markdown Document.
- Support private pasted images.
- Add expiry and complete deletion.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the navigation module established by markshare-yis for About, Privacy, and Acceptable Use destinations. Do not add route checks directly to App.
- The navigation module owns route recognition, precedence, URL construction, and unavailable outcomes. Unknown paths must not fall through to the Editor.
- Keep Share Link privacy behaviour local to the Document lifecycle and navigation modules: generic unavailable results, private metadata, no edit-capability leakage, and no content-derived public preview data.
- Analytics, logging, referrer, indexing, and rate-limit controls must be verified at their observable seams rather than inferred from configuration text alone.
- Public-information content may be static, but its route meaning belongs to the same navigation test surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Share Links expose no Document title or content to indexing, previews, referrers, analytics, or application logs.
- Creation and image upload are rate-limited and the public-information destinations describe the agreed behaviour.
- Public-information, Share Link, Edit Link, and unknown routes share one navigation test surface; unknown paths never open the Editor.
- Privacy and abuse controls are verified through observable outcomes and deployment configuration checks.
- Tests, type checking, lint, production build, and production-like verification pass.
close_reason: Share Links stay generic to crawlers and referrers, creation and image upload are rate-limited, and About/Privacy/Acceptable use describe that behaviour.

title: Production-readiness and handover
description:
## What to build

Verify the finished MarkShare flows end to end, including accessibility and mobile behaviour; complete production deployment configuration; and document manual InstantDB export and recovery steps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The supported creation, editing, reading, image, expiry, deletion, privacy, and theme flows are verified in a production-like deployment.
- [ ] An owner can follow concise guidance to export data and understand the recovery limits of version one.

## Blocked by

- Make the editor resilient and responsive.
- Support private pasted images.
- Add expiry and complete deletion.
- Apply privacy, abuse, and public-information controls.
acceptance_criteria: MarkShare is ready to launch and hand over.

title: Support private pasted images
description:
## What to build

Authors can paste or drag PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images into a Document. MarkShare stores them privately in InstantDB, inserts Markdown automatically, and serves them only through an available Share Link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pasting or dropping a supported image inserts it into the editor and renders it for readers.
- [ ] The 5 MB per-image and 20 images per-Document limits are enforced, and image access does not become public through a standalone file URL.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Deliver the complete Markdown reading experience.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the deep Document lifecycle module from markshare-ntg for image ownership, limits, persistence, and capability-controlled retrieval.
- UI modules must not call InstantDB image storage directly or interpret Share/Edit capability rules.
- Feed safe Document-scoped image references into the shared Markdown interpretation module from markshare-txp; do not create a second rendering policy for images.
- A standalone file URL must never become an alternative seam that bypasses Document availability.
- Test image lifecycle outcomes through the Document lifecycle interface and rendered image safety through the Markdown interpretation interface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pasting or dropping PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF inserts a Document-scoped Markdown reference and renders through the shared interpretation module.
- The 5 MB per-image and 20-images-per-Document limits are enforced in the Document lifecycle module.
- Image retrieval follows Document capability and availability rules; standalone file access cannot bypass them.
- UI modules do not access InstantDB image persistence directly.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Make the editor resilient and responsive
description:
## What to build

The editor provides side-by-side Write and Preview on desktop, Edit and Preview tabs on mobile, browser-local recovery for unpublished work, and import of existing Markdown files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The authoring flow is usable on current desktop and mobile browsers.
- [ ] Unsaved local work recovers after an accidental close, but public content changes only after Save changes.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Deliver the complete Markdown reading experience.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Deepen the Editor session rather than extracting isolated event helpers.
- Keep draft state, published state, local recovery, Markdown import, save transitions, retry behaviour, pane state, split invariants, and cleanup rules together behind one module interface.
- DOM-specific pointer capture, CSS custom properties, body-class mutation, local storage, and breakpoint behaviour stay inside the implementation.
- Browser dependencies are local-substitutable with jsdom, local storage stand-ins, and synthetic pointer/keyboard events. Do not expose browser adapters through the external interface.
- Test complete session transitions and observable interaction outcomes: recover, import, edit, save, failure/retry, tab switch, split clamping, keyboard increments, reset, and drag cleanup.
- Replace CSS-string assertions when an observable behaviour test covers the same rule. Retain only exact stylesheet contracts that cannot be observed reliably in jsdom.
- Isolated drag, clamp, or word-count helper modules are shallow and do not satisfy this design.

- Desktop Write/Preview, mobile Edit/Preview tabs, local draft recovery, Markdown import, and explicit save work end to end.
- Unsaved work recovers after an accidental close while public Reader content changes only after save.
- Split dragging, clamping, keyboard movement, reset, pointer cancellation, and body-class cleanup have observable interaction tests.
- Editor session tests survive internal refactors and do not depend on CSS source-text matching where behaviour is observable.
- Tests, type checking, lint, production build, and documented responsive browser checks pass.
