title: Bootstrap the MarkShare application
description:
## What to build

A deployable MarkShare shell on Vercel with InstantDB configuration, the agreed calm visual
foundation, Light/Dark/System theme selection, and a responsive home page that starts document
creation.

The visual foundation is no longer open to interpretation. It was settled by a three-variant UI
prototype (Split Desk / Paper / Console); **Split Desk won**. The full, authoritative interface
specification — colour tokens, typography, layout metrics, component specs, responsive rules and
interaction behaviour — is in the Design section of this issue, and the working reference
implementation is `prototype/ui/markshare-ui-prototype.html` with notes in
`prototype/ui/README.md`.

Build the design system and the app shell here. Later issues fill the shell in:
`markshare-xpb` (create and read), `markshare-txp` (rendering pipeline), `markshare-yis`
(edit links and explicit publishing), `markshare-2ck` (editor responsiveness and drafts).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The application runs locally and can deploy to Vercel with its required configuration
      documented.
- [ ] The home page provides a clear Create a document path and persists the selected System,
      Light, or Dark theme.
- [ ] The design tokens in the Design section exist as the single source of truth for colour,
      typography, spacing and radii, and both themes are driven by one `data-theme` switch.
- [ ] The shell fills the viewport at every window size with no page-level scroll and no
      horizontal overflow: verified at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420 and 320 wide.
- [ ] The two documented breakpoints behave as specified — 900px (panes to tabs) and 620px
      (condensed top bar).

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
design:
# MarkShare interface specification — authoritative

Settled by prototype round 1 (Split Desk vs Paper vs Console). Split Desk won. Reference
implementation: `prototype/ui/markshare-ui-prototype.html`. Screenshots: `prototype/ui/shots/`.

The prototype is throwaway code — copy the *design*, not the implementation. Anything below marked
PROTOTYPE ONLY must not be carried across.

## 1. Design tokens

Both themes are driven by one attribute on `<html>`: `data-theme="light" | "dark"`. The stored
preference is `system | light | dark`; `system` resolves against
`matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` and must re-resolve live when the OS setting changes.

Light:

    --paper      #faf9f6   app background, write surface
    --surface    #ffffff   bars, preview, cards
    --surface-2  #f3f1ec   hover fills, segmented control track
    --sunken     #efece5   code blocks, link boxes, inline code
    --ink        #232019   primary text
    --ink-soft   #5d574c   secondary text, code text
    --ink-faint  #8f887a   labels, metadata, footer
    --line       #e6e1d6   structural borders
    --line-soft  #f0ece3   internal dividers, table rules
    --accent     #3f6f5c   primary buttons, active divider, checked boxes
    --accent-soft #e4efe9  accent chips
    --accent-ink #2c5344   accent text on soft accent
    --warn       #8a5a2b   unsaved state
    --danger     #8f3a3a   delete

Dark:

    --paper      #15161a
    --surface    #1b1d22
    --surface-2  #22252b
    --sunken     #101114
    --ink        #e9e7e0
    --ink-soft   #a9a49a
    --ink-faint  #7b756b
    --line       #2c3038
    --line-soft  #23262c
    --accent     #7fb79c
    --accent-soft #1f3129
    --accent-ink #a9d4c1
    --warn       #c69a63
    --danger     #d98a8a

Shared: `--radius: 10px`;
`--shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(35,32,25,.05), 0 8px 24px rgba(35,32,25,.06)` (dark:
`0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.35)`).

Primary button text is `#fff` in light and `#10231c` in dark — do not use `--paper`.

## 2. Typography

- Interface and rendered document: **Inter**, weights 400/500/600/700, with
  `font-feature-settings: "cv05" 1, "ss03" 1` (single-storey l, curved r). Self-host it; do not
  ship a Google Fonts request to production. Fallback: `ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "Segoe UI",
  system-ui, sans-serif`.
- Markdown source, link URLs and metadata: `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`.
  Column alignment matters in tables and code, so the Write pane is never proportional.
- Base: 15px / 1.5.
- Rendered document: h1 1.9em/1.2 weight 650 tracking -0.022em; h2 1.32em weight 640 tracking
  -0.014em with 1.9em top margin; h3 1.08em weight 650; h4 1em weight 650 in `--ink-soft`.
  Paragraph bottom margin 1.05em.
- Measure: preview column `max-width: 62ch` centred; reader column `max-width: 66ch` at 16px.

## 3. Shell layout — author surface

Single full-height column, top to bottom:

1. **App bar**, 56px, `--surface`, 1px `--line` bottom border. Left: 20px rounded mark
   (`--accent`, radius 6px) + "MarkShare" at weight 700, tracking -0.015em. Then a 1px `--line`
   separator and the document title (weight 560, truncates with ellipsis) followed by the save-state
   chip. Right, in order: theme toggle (quiet), Share (secondary), Save changes (primary).
2. **Tab strip**, only below 900px — a segmented control (Edit / Preview) on a `--sunken` track,
   3px padding, 9px radius; the active segment is `--surface` with `--shadow`.
3. **Pane row**, fills remaining height. CSS grid:
   `grid-template-columns: var(--split, 50%) 7px 1fr`.
   - Write pane: 40px head ("WRITE" label + formatting tools, right-aligned), then a full-height
     textarea, `--paper`, mono 13.4px / 1.75, padding 22px 24px.
   - Divider: the 7px middle column. See §5.
   - Preview pane: 40px head ("PREVIEW" label + a mono note reading "matches share link" or
     "not yet published"), then the scrolling rendered document on `--surface`, padding 32px 40px.
4. **Status footer**, 32px, 11.5px `--ink-faint`: word count, `n/20` images, expiry state, and the
   share URL pushed right in mono.

Labels ("WRITE", "PREVIEW", field labels) are 11px, weight 700, uppercase, 0.06em tracking,
`--ink-faint`.

## 4. Shell layout — reader surface

What a share-link recipient sees. 52px bar: mark, document title, a "Read only" chip, then expiry
text, Download .md, theme toggle. Below it the rendered document scrolls **inside its own
container** (not the page), padding 56px 24px 120px, 66ch measure at 16px.

No editing affordances may appear on this surface. Nothing here may leak the edit link.

## 5. The resizable divider

- Grid column of 7px. The visible line is a 1px `--line` rule centred in it, plus a resting grip:
  3px × 28px, radius 3px, `--ink-faint` at 0.5 opacity, so it reads as draggable before hover.
- Hover / focus / drag: the rule thickens to 3px and turns `--accent`; the resting grip fades out.
- Cursor `col-resize`; `touch-action: none` so pointer drags work on touch devices.
- **Drag** sets the split as a percentage of the pane row's width, clamped to **22%–78%**.
- **Double-click** resets to **50%**.
- **Keyboard**: it is a real `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`,
  `aria-valuenow/min/max`, in the tab order. `←`/`→` nudge 2%, with Shift 10%; `Home` resets.
  `aria-valuenow` updates as it moves.
- Dragging must not re-render the document: write the percentage to a CSS custom property on the
  pane row and update state without a redraw. Add a body-level `user-select: none; cursor:
  col-resize` for the duration of the drag and remove it on pointerup.
- The split position survives re-renders. Below 900px the divider is `display: none`.

## 6. Responsive rules

The shell owns the window. `html, body { height: 100%; overflow: hidden }`, the app root is
`height: 100%`, and the shell is `min-height/max-height: 100dvh`. Every scroll happens inside a
pane. The page itself must never scroll — that is what pushed the app bar off-screen in an earlier
build.

- **≥ 900px** — two panes, divider live.
- **< 900px** — divider hidden, grid collapses to one column, Edit / Preview tabs shown, only the
  selected pane rendered. Preview padding drops to 24px 20px.
- **< 620px** — Share collapses to an icon (↗), "Save changes" becomes "Save", the wordmark is
  hidden so the document title keeps its space, and the "Saved" chip is dropped. **The amber
  unsaved dot must always survive** — explicit publishing depends on it being visible. The footer
  hides the share URL; the reader bar hides the expiry text.

Verify at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420 and 320 wide: shell fills the viewport, no
page scroll, no horizontal overflow.

## 7. Components

- **Button**: radius 8px, padding 7px 13px, 13.5px weight 500, 1px `--line` border on `--surface`;
  hover fills `--surface-2`. Small: 5px 9px / 12.5px. Primary: `--accent` fill and border. Quiet:
  transparent border and fill, `--ink-soft` text.
- **Chip / pill**: radius 999px, padding 3px 9px, 11.5px weight 600. Saved = `--surface-2` on
  `--line-soft`. Unsaved = transparent fill, `--warn` text and border, with a 6px `--warn` dot.
- **Link box** (share / edit link): `--sunken` fill, 1px `--line-soft`, radius 8px, padding
  9px 11px; mono URL truncating with ellipsis, Copy button on the right.
- **Publish modal**: scrim `rgba(20,18,14,.42)`; card `min(520px, 100%)`, radius 14px, padding
  24px, `--shadow`. Contents in order: heading "Your document is live", the line "Anyone with the
  share link can read it. No one can change it.", the read-only share link, the private edit link
  labelled "keep it safe", expiry set/remove, then Delete document (danger, quiet) and Done.
  Clicking the scrim closes; clicking the card does not; `Esc` closes.
- **Toast**: centred pill above the bottom edge, `--ink` fill with `--paper` text, ~1.9s. It must
  not own rendering — an action fired while an earlier toast is up still has to redraw.

## 8. Behaviour the shell must get right

- **Explicit publishing.** The draft is allowed to run ahead of the published document. The
  save-state chip flips to "Unsaved changes" **as the author types**, not on blur or on save, and
  the preview head switches to "not yet published". `⌘S` / `Ctrl+S` saves.
- **Title rule.** The document title is the first `# ` heading, else "Untitled document":
  `md.split("\n").find(l => l.startsWith("# "))?.slice(2).trim()`.
- **Theme.** Toggle cycles system → light → dark. Persist the choice; resolve `system` live.
- **Reader shows the saved version**, never the draft.
- Typing must not lose caret position or scroll position, and must not re-render the textarea.

## 9. Not covered by the prototype

- **The home page / creation entry point** in this issue's scope was never prototyped. Build it
  from these tokens: same 56px bar, one clear "Create a document" primary action, theme control
  present. Anything beyond that is a fresh design decision — do not invent a dashboard.
- The Markdown pipeline itself belongs to `markshare-txp`: sanitised GitHub-flavoured Markdown,
  no raw HTML, strict Mermaid. The prototype's renderer is a toy for layout only.

## 10. PROTOTYPE ONLY — do not port

Fake in-memory document and links; fake copy-to-clipboard; the decorative B / I / H / link / code /
image toolbar (no behaviour behind it); the floating "PROTOTYPE" bar and its Author/Reader toggle;
`innerHTML` re-rendering; the toy Markdown renderer; the Google Fonts `<link>`.

## 11. Known open questions

- Preview scroll does not follow the cursor; with a wide Write pane the two sides drift. Decide
  whether scroll sync is in scope for version one.
- The formatting toolbar needs real behaviour, or should be dropped from the first build.
- Whether the split position should persist per browser (localStorage) or reset each session.
acceptance_criteria: The deployable themed application shell and creation entry point work end to end, built on the design tokens and responsive rules recorded in the Design section, with no page-level scroll or horizontal overflow at any window size.
close_reason: Implemented by commits 9ac408e and 295734a; responsive shell, theme persistence, documented setup, and Split Desk design are present. Verified 2026-08-13: 19 tests, type checking, and lint pass.

description:

Anyone can write Markdown in the browser, publish it without an account, receive a hard-to-guess Share Link, and open that link to read the rendered Document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publishing creates a persistent Document and a unique read-only Share Link.
- [ ] A visitor with the Share Link can read the rendered Document, while an unknown or unavailable link does not disclose content.

## Blocked by

title: Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing
description:
## What to build

Authors receive a private Edit Link; the same browser remembers edit access; Share Link recipients remain read-only; edits publish only when the author saves; authors can delete a Document or replace a leaked Edit Link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Share Link cannot modify a Document; an Edit Link can modify, revoke, or replace it.
- [ ] The author must save changes explicitly before readers see them, and returning in the same browser restores edit access.

## Blocked by

- Create and read a basic Markdown Document.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- This work depends on markshare-ntg. Extend the deep Document lifecycle module; do not reintroduce raw InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, timestamps, or capability rules in UI modules.
- The lifecycle module owns Share Link versus Edit Link capability meaning, explicit publication, revocation, rotation, deletion requests, and domain outcomes.
- Establish saved-versus-draft transitions in the Editor session so the Reader always sees the saved version. Keep transition rules together rather than scattering them across event handlers.
- Once the exact Edit Link path grammar is chosen, deepen Share/Edit Link routing: one navigation module owns recognition, capability interpretation, URL construction, and browser-history behaviour. Unknown non-root routes must resolve as unavailable, not as the Editor.
- Browser history is local-substitutable; keep browser details internal rather than exposing a new port.
- Test lifecycle, capability, saved-versus-draft, route round trips, malformed paths, and unknown paths through stable interfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
- Share Links remain read-only; Edit Links can edit, save, revoke or rotate access, and request deletion.
- The same browser restores edit access without disclosing the Edit Link to Share Link readers.
- Draft changes remain private until explicit save, and Reader output always reflects the saved version.
- UI modules do not construct InstantDB operations or capability rule parameters.
- Share/Edit route recognition and construction have one test surface; malformed and unknown routes disclose nothing and never open the Editor.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7: private Edit Links, explicit save, same-browser remembered access, rotate, and delete.

title: Settle when an open Edit Link stops showing an expired document
description:
## Why

The Share Link route schedules a re-render at the expiry instant, so a reader watching a document expire sees it become unavailable. The Edit Link route schedules nothing. Expiry is decided inside the Document lifecycle at read time, so with no re-render nothing re-asks, and an editor already open keeps showing a document that has expired.

Loading and unavailable are written twice in two different shapes: the Share route branches on the lifecycle outcome, the Editor branches on its published edit capability matching the route.

The product answer is not recorded anywhere. An author holding the Edit Link may reasonably keep editing past expiry, or may reasonably be told the document is gone. Today the code answers "keep editing" by omission rather than by decision.

## What to build

Record what an open Edit Link does at the expiry instant, then let both routes reach that answer through one interface. Whichever answer wins, the expiry re-render and the loading and unavailable outcomes belong in one module rather than once per route.

## Scope limits

Keep expiry policy, the never-expires default, and the unavailable page copy as they are. Leave Share versus Edit meaning closed. Schedule against the known expiry instant rather than polling. Leave the Editor workspace interface to markshare-6sb, which assumes App still routes the edit capability in.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

• Decided 16 Aug: the document is gone. An Edit Link open at the expiry instant shows the same unavailable page a Share Link shows. Implement this; do not reopen it.
• One module takes a route and answers loading, unavailable, or the document. Share and Edit read the same three outcomes.
• The expiry re-render is scheduled inside that module, once, for both link kinds. Expiry stays decided in the Document lifecycle; the module only forces the re-ask.
• The unsaved local recovery draft survives expiry. Expiry removes access to the published Document, not the author's local text. Leave the recovery entry in local storage when the route turns unavailable.
• The module interface is the test surface. Cover a document that expires while open, under each link kind, including one with unsaved changes.
• Existing deep-link outcomes hold: unknown share id, truncated share id, and deleted document keep the same unavailable answer.
• Observed on 560e294 by reading the routes. The asymmetry was not reproduced in a browser; confirm it before treating the current behaviour as a defect.
acceptance_criteria:
• An Edit Link open at the expiry instant shows the same unavailable page as a Share Link.
• Both routes obtain loading, unavailable, and the document through one interface.
• The expiry re-render is scheduled in one module, not once per route.
• A document that expires while open reaches the unavailable page, proven for both link kinds at that interface.
• An author with unsaved changes at the expiry instant keeps their local recovery draft; it is not cleared by the switch to unavailable.
• Unknown, truncated, and deleted share links keep their existing unavailable outcome.
• Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
notes:
DECISION 16 Aug (darrenbryant): the document is gone.

An Edit Link open at the expiry instant shows the same unavailable page a Share Link shows. Both link kinds reach that outcome the same way. This closes the open product question; implement it rather than reopening it.

Consequence the implementer must handle, not re-decide: the editor holds an unsaved local recovery draft keyed by the edit capability. Switching to the unavailable page must not destroy what the author typed. Leave the recovery draft in local storage — expiry removes access to the published Document, not the author's local text.

title: Put the abuse limiter behind its own seam
description:
## Why

Public write limits shipped on 15 Aug, after the last architecture pass. The limiter landed inside the Document lifecycle module rather than beside it. Six names now sit on the lifecycle interface — CREATE_DOCUMENT_LIMIT, UPLOAD_IMAGE_LIMIT, AbuseLimits, AbuseStore, createMemoryAbuseStore, createLocalStorageAbuseStore — plus four private window helpers. Save asks the limiter two questions. Callers must learn six names to configure it.

Two adapters already exist, memory and localStorage, so the seam is real rather than hypothetical. It is just drawn in the wrong place.

createDocumentLifecycle now takes six positional parameters, four of them optional. The one production call site passes positional undefined twice to reach the sixth.

## What to build

Concentrate abuse limiting behind one module interface: ask whether a publish has capacity, and record it once the publish succeeds. Window length, pruning, storage keys, and both stores stay implementation. The lifecycle constructor takes named options.

## Scope limits

Keep the limits, the window length, and the set of limited actions exactly as they are; this is a seam move, not a policy change. Leave the persistence and removal seams to markshare-0wy. Keep limiting client-side in this issue. Keep the limiter a plain module, not a React hook.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

• One abuse-limits module owns both questions: has this publish kind capacity for N at time T, and record N of this kind at time T. Window length, pruning, the two storage keys, and both stores are implementation.
• Two adapters justify the seam: memory in tests, localStorage in the browser. Both stay behind the limiter interface. The lifecycle interface names neither.
• Only a successful publish consumes quota. That rule shipped in 41f3ab9 and must survive the move unchanged.
• The limiter interface is the test surface for window behaviour. Move the window and pruning tests onto it. The lifecycle keeps the outcome tests that prove a rate-limited save publishes no Document. Replace, do not layer.
• createDocumentLifecycle accepts persistence plus one named options object. No call site passes positional undefined.
• markshare-0wy edits the same constructor for the persistence and removal seams. Landing this first means that work starts from named options rather than a six-parameter list.
acceptance_criteria:
• Rate-limit names leave the Document lifecycle interface; callers configure limiting through the abuse-limits module.
• Both storage adapters sit behind the limiter interface; the lifecycle interface names neither.
• Only a successful publish consumes quota, proven at the limiter interface.
• A rate-limited save publishes no Document, proven at the lifecycle interface.
• createDocumentLifecycle takes named options; no call site passes positional undefined.
• Window and pruning tests live at the limiter interface and replace the lifecycle copies rather than adding a second suite.
• Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: [bug] Give the browser chrome the reader's theme, not a fixed light one
description:
## Problem

index.html ships `<meta name="theme-color" content="#faf9f6" />`. That value is `--paper` from the light `:root` block in src/styles/tokens.css, and nothing ever changes it. A visitor on Dark gets a light address bar above dark content on mobile Safari and Chrome, on every route, forever.

This is not the first-paint flash markshare-lkf fixed. It never flashes. It is simply always wrong for half the visitors.

Found during review of markshare-lkf.

## Expected

The browser chrome follows the same resolved theme the page does, including a stored preference, not only the OS setting.

## Notes

Two shapes are possible and they are not equivalent:

- Paired `<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">` tags. No script, but it follows the OS only, so a visitor on a dark OS who chose Light still gets a dark bar.
- One more line in the boot script in src/theme.ts, plus an update when the theme control cycles. Follows the real preference, but it puts two design-token colours into JavaScript, where they can drift from tokens.css. Decide how those colours stay single-source before writing it.

## Out of scope

- The cycle order, the storage key, or where the theme control appears.
- Any other token leaving tokens.css.

title: Stop the light flash before the theme applies on a full page load
description:
## Problem

index.html hard-codes <html data-theme="light">, and nothing sets the real theme until React mounts. A visitor whose stored preference is Dark, or whose OS is dark while on System, gets a flash of light chrome on every full page load.

This affects Home, the Editor, and Share Links alike. It is not specific to the reader.

Found during review of markshare-0qt, which gave Share Link readers a theme control. That bead fixed the missing control. The first-paint flash is older and wider, so it is its own piece of work.

## Expected

The first painted frame already carries the resolved theme. No flash, on any route, on a cold load.

## Notes

The usual shape is a small blocking inline script in index.html that reads the same storage key and prefers-color-scheme, then sets data-theme and colorScheme before the first paint. It must read the same key and the same resolve rule as src/theme.ts, not a second copy of the logic.

## Out of scope

- Changing the cycle order, the storage key, or where the control appears.
- Server-side rendering.
notes: PR https://github.com/djfbryant/md-viewer/pull/16 opened 2026-08-16 on branch fix/markshare-lkf-theme-flash. Vercel preview deploy passing. Bead stays open until the PR merges. Discovered markshare-ksn (fixed light theme-color meta) during review; deliberately not fixed here.

title: Ordinary flowcharts hit the Mermaid safety fallback
description:
## Problem

A normal left-to-right flowchart in Preview is shown as a safety failure:

> This diagram could not be rendered safely.

The source is ordinary Mermaid: a User node, an Intent? decision, Code/Chat/Agent branches, and a Review loop with Accept and Reject. There is no click handler and no javascript URL. A reader should see the diagram. Instead they get the source in a fallback panel, as if MarkShare blocked it.

That copy is used for every Mermaid failure: blocked input, a renderer exception, and sanitized SVG with no viewBox. An everyday architecture diagram and a hostile click handler look the same.

## Reproduction

1. Create a document.
2. Paste this fence:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[User] --> B{Intent?}
    B -->|Code| C[Editor]
    B -->|Chat| D[Composer]
    B -->|Agent| E[Cursor Agent]
    C --> F[LSP]
    D --> G[Context]
    E --> H[Tools]
    F --> I[Model]
    G --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J[Apply]
    J --> K[Review]
    K -->|Accept| L[Done]
    K -->|Reject| M[Retry]
    M --> E
```

3. Open Preview.
4. Observed in the annotated Preview: the safety fallback and the source, not the SVG.
5. Rechecked the same source against Mermaid 11.16.1 with MarkShare's strict config: it parses, it draws, and Preview can show it. The remaining defect is that any renderer miss still uses the safety caption, and tests mock Mermaid so this flowchart is never proven.

## Expected

This flowchart renders. The safety fallback is for actually hostile Mermaid, not for a decision diamond or a labelled edge. If Mermaid cannot draw a harmless diagram, say that it could not be displayed and show the source. Do not call that a safety failure.

## Out of scope

- Changing Markdown safety, raw HTML rejection, or Share Link privacy
- New diagram types beyond proving this flowchart class
- Author-configurable Mermaid security
design:
## Authoritative diagnosis

The annotated Preview figure was mermaid-fallback with caption This diagram could not be rendered safely. The source is an ordinary flowchart: decision diamond with a question mark, edge labels, spaces in node text, and a retry cycle. It is not interactive.

MarkShare uses one invalid path for three different failures: the input filter, mermaid.render throwing, and sanitized SVG with no usable viewBox. Authors only see the safety sentence, so a renderer miss looks like a policy block.

The input filter allows this source. It rejects line-leading %%{, line-leading click, and javascript:. Verified 2026-08-14 against Mermaid 11.16.1 with the production initialize (securityLevel strict, htmlLabels false, suppressErrorRendering true): parse succeeds, render returns an SVG with viewBox 0 0 1628.859375 243.75, and the second DOMPurify SVG-profile pass keeps geometry. The same source then drew in the live Preview, including Intent?, Cursor Agent, Accept/Reject, and the cycle back to the agent.

So this paste is not unsafe. If Preview still showed the fallback, mermaid.render or normalize threw and the catch-all caption blamed safety. Current unit tests mock mermaid.render, so they stay green even when a real flowchart cannot draw.

Do not treat every %%{init} as a security bypass without checking the locked keys. securityLevel is already in mermaid.initialize secure. htmlLabels is not. Keep htmlLabels false and locked if init directives are allowed. Do not set securityLevel to loose.

## Representative source

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[User] --> B{Intent?}
    B -->|Code| C[Editor]
    B -->|Chat| D[Composer]
    B -->|Agent| E[Cursor Agent]
    C --> F[LSP]
    D --> G[Context]
    E --> H[Tools]
    F --> I[Model]
    G --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J[Apply]
    J --> K[Review]
    K -->|Accept| L[Done]
    K -->|Reject| M[Retry]
    M --> E
```

## Implementation contract

- Keep one Mermaid path for Preview and Share Link.
- Prove this flowchart with a real mermaid.render, not the stub that returns a 100 by 100 SVG.
- Hostile input still fails closed. Ordinary flowcharts must not.
- Fallback copy must distinguish a blocked diagram from one Mermaid could not draw.
acceptance_criteria:
- The representative LR flowchart below draws in Preview and on a Share Link. It is not shown as a safety fallback.
- click handlers, javascript: URLs, and init that tries to loosen security still fall back and never reach mermaid.render.
- A diagram Mermaid cannot parse uses copy that does not accuse safety. Hostile input can keep safety wording.
- A real Mermaid render of this flowchart is covered by tests, not a mocked mermaid.render that always returns a stub SVG.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Share Links have no theme control for the reader
description:
## Problem

Home and Editor let you cycle System, Light, and Dark. A published Share Link does not. The document still uses whatever theme that browser already stored, usually the author's if they open their own link, or System for a first-time visitor. There is no control to change it.

That is disjointed. A Share Link is a reading surface for someone else. Appearance should belong to the person looking at it, not to whoever last used MarkShare in that browser with no way out.

The Split Desk reader bar already called for this: mark, title, Read only, expiry, Download .md, theme toggle. The toggle never landed on the live Reader.

## Reproduction

1. On Home or in the Editor, cycle theme to Light or Dark.
2. Save a Document and open its Share Link, including as a full page load.
3. The Reader keeps that theme.
4. The reader bar has expiry and Download .md, but no theme control, so you cannot switch to System or the other theme.

A first-time visitor with no stored preference gets System, which is the right default, but they still cannot choose Light or Dark.

## Expected

Anyone viewing a live Share Link can cycle System → Light → Dark, same order as Home and Editor. With no stored preference, start on System and follow the OS. Persist the choice in that browser only. The URL stays a document link, not a theme link.

## Out of scope

- Per-document or author-chosen appearance
- A separate theme for Preview versus Reader
- Changing Mermaid, Markdown, or privacy behaviour
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Theme remains a browser preference. Do not encode Light, Dark, or System in the Share Link, Document, or query string.
- A visitor with no stored preference starts on System and resolves it live against prefers-color-scheme, including while the OS setting changes.
- The Reader bar specified in markshare-9yf already includes the theme toggle after Download .md. Wire that control into the Share Link chrome. Loading and unavailable Reader pages need it too, otherwise a broken or expired link is the one place a visitor cannot leave a locked theme.
- Reuse the existing cycle, persist, and resolve behaviour. Do not add a second theme store or a Share-Link-only preference.
- Keep Share Links read-only. Theme must not grow an Edit control, leak Edit Link capability, or change published Markdown.
- Tests must open a Share Link (not only Home) and prove the control is present, cycles, persists, and that System still follows the OS.
acceptance_criteria:
- The published Share Link reader bar includes the same System / Light / Dark theme control as Home and Editor.
- A reader with no stored preference starts on System and can cycle System → Light → Dark.
- Changing theme on a Share Link persists in that browser and does not travel with the URL.
- Loading, available, unavailable, and expired Share Link pages all expose the control.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Shrink the persistence interface
description:
## Why

The Document lifecycle module is already deep. Its persistence seam is not. `DocumentPersistence` still exposes React hooks, Instant date wire types, an `editId` on upload that Instant cannot use, and two file ID spaces that share a field name. App tests invented a third adapter. The cron handler calls `cleanupDueDocuments` instead of `lifecycle.cleanup()`.

Re-deepening the whole lifecycle would not fix this. The Instant shape leaked into the interface.

## What to build

Shrink the persistence interface so Instant query DSL, hook loading, and path lookup stay inside the client adapter. Tests reuse the memory adapter already used by lifecycle tests. Give the admin cleanup path a lifecycle that includes a removal adapter, instead of a parallel helper.

## Scope limits

Do not reopen Document lifecycle capability rules, Share vs Edit meaning, or expiry policy. Do not collapse `DocumentPersistence` and `DocumentRemovalStore` into one interface; Instant forces two SDKs. Do not add a second Instant client in App. Do not treat `instant.perms.ts` string snapshots as proof of Storage create.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Instant `useQuery`, `transact`, `uploadFile`, and `lookup('path')` stay inside the Instant client adapter. They are not part of the lifecycle interface callers must learn.
- Two adapters already justify the persistence seam: Instant in production, memory in tests. Delete the App-test mock of `documentLifecycle`. Replace, do not layer.
- `DocumentRemovalStore` remains a separate seam. Client `$files.delete` is false; admin cleanup needs the admin SDK. Two adapters: Instant admin in production, the same memory store in tests.
- Cron must go through a lifecycle that has a removal adapter, or an equivalent factory that returns the same cleanup outcomes. Do not keep `cleanupDueDocuments` as a second public entry next to unused `lifecycle.cleanup()`.
- Client image ids (path suffix) and admin `$files.id` must not be treated as the same array. Hide that difference inside the adapters.
- A denied `$files` create fails Save and leaves no published Document. That test belongs at the lifecycle interface with a persistence adapter that rejects create.
- `scheduled-cleanup.ts` status mapping may be inlined into the cron handler. It has one caller. Do not add a new HTTP module for it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Instant query DSL, React hooks, and path lookup stay inside the Instant client adapter, not on the lifecycle caller interface.
- App tests use the memory persistence adapter; the third documentLifecycle mock is gone.
- Cron cleanup goes through a lifecycle that includes a removal adapter, not a parallel cleanupDueDocuments entry next to unused lifecycle.cleanup().
- DocumentPersistence and DocumentRemovalStore remain separate seams with production and test adapters.
- A persistence adapter that rejects image create fails Save and leaves no published Document, proven at the lifecycle interface.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
notes:
Architecture review 16 Aug — two points for whoever picks this up.

1. Where the test seam goes. This issue says delete the App-test mock of documentLifecycle and use the memory adapter. App.tsx still imports the documentLifecycle singleton directly, so no adapter can be handed in without vi.mock. Four test files now reach past App this way: AppDocument.test.tsx (772 lines, the largest file in the repo), editor-session.test.tsx, markdown.mermaid-render.test.tsx, instant-document-persistence.test.ts. Choosing where that seam sits — a prop on App, or a context — is part of this issue. useEditorSession already accepts a lifecycle, so the seam exists one level too deep.

2. Which cleanup entry survives. This issue chose lifecycle.cleanup() and dropping cleanupDueDocuments as a public entry. Current state on 560e294 is the reverse: api/cleanup.ts calls cleanupDueDocuments directly, the browser lifecycle is built with no removal adapter so cleanup() can only answer not-configured, and its only callers are two cases in document-lifecycle.test.ts. Both directions collapse the duplication. Recording the current state so the recorded direction is implemented rather than re-argued.

Also note markshare-24r moves the abuse limiter out of the same constructor. Landing it first means this work starts from named options instead of six positional parameters.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #17 (refactor/markshare-0wy-shrink-persistence-interface). Closed past the markshare-6yx blocker: the persistence-seam work landed first and 6yx's App-test and denied-create criteria are already satisfied by it.

title: Hide the Mermaid expand session
description:
## Why

Preview matches Share Link for expanded Mermaid only because App remembers to wrap both in `RenderedDocument`. That adapter is 15 lines. Callers of `MarkdownView` must still learn a two-phase protocol: fire `onMermaidExpand`, then pass `openMermaidId` back so the inline SVG unmounts. The duplicate-ID invariant lives in App, not in Markdown interpretation.

The overlay itself is already deep. The leak is the expand session sitting in App.

## What to build

Hide the Mermaid expand session inside Markdown interpretation. `MarkdownView` owns open and close of the viewer. Keep `mermaid-viewer.tsx` as an internal seam with its own tests. Delete `RenderedDocument`.

## Scope limits

Do not merge `mermaid-viewer.tsx` into `markdown.tsx`. Do not extract inline `MermaidDiagram` as a public module. Do not add a second Mermaid renderer. Do not pass lane widths into `MarkdownView` to dodge CSS class coupling; that would widen the interface.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Markdown interpretation remains one shared module. Preview and Reader call `interpretMarkdown` plus `MarkdownView` only. Expand/focus/duplicate-SVG rules are implementation, not part of the external interface.
- `MermaidViewer` stays a deep overlay behind an internal seam. Own tests may remain at that seam. App must not import it.
- Drop `onMermaidExpand`, `openMermaidId`, and `MermaidExpandRequest` from the MarkdownView interface once the view owns the session.
- Un-export sizing/overflow helpers (`mermaidSizingDecision`, `mermaidOverflowCue`) if view tests already cover those outcomes. Replace isolated helper tests; do not layer both suites.
- Geometry for Fit in the viewer should trust the SVG Markdown already normalized. Do not keep two parse fallbacks that can drift.
- Layout class names `.preview` and `.reader-content` as measurement inputs are a leak. Prefer Markdown-owned markers or nearest-container observation inside the implementation, without widening the interface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preview and Reader call MarkdownView without an App expand adapter; RenderedDocument is gone.
- MarkdownView owns open and close of the expanded viewer. App does not import MermaidViewer.
- Duplicate-SVG unmount and focus restoration remain correct and are proven through MarkdownView plus viewer tests.
- mermaid-viewer.tsx stays a separate internal overlay; it is not merged into markdown.tsx.
- Existing strict Mermaid safety, sanitization, and Preview/Reader equivalence remain intact.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
notes:
Architecture review 16 Aug — this issue's scope limit was re-tested and holds.

markdown.tsx is 548 lines carrying three concerns: Markdown interpretation, ~230 lines of Mermaid presentation, and private image resolution. Its interface has 11 exports, 7 of them Mermaid: mermaidSizingDecision, mermaidOverflowCue, MERMAID_MINIMUM_SCALE, MermaidGeometry, MermaidSizingDecision, MermaidExpandRequest, MermaidExpandHandler.

The review considered extracting a public mermaid-diagram module and rejected it, matching the scope limit already recorded here. The Mermaid bugs since — 12f9ce7 (ordinary flowcharts off the safety fallback), 6a9fd30 (labels and expanded viewer on the document theme), ee49423 — all sat in the render and fallback path, not in the sizing maths. Extracting the maths as a public module would not have caught any of them.

The part that stands is already recorded here: un-export mermaidSizingDecision and mermaidOverflowCue once view tests cover those outcomes. markdown.test.tsx:334-351 is the isolated helper suite to replace.

title: Pasted image test fails only in the full suite run
description:
## Problem

`src/AppDocument.test.tsx > basic anonymous documents > pastes a private image into the editor and renders it on the share link` fails when the whole suite runs, but passes on its own.

- `npx vitest run src/AppDocument.test.tsx -t "pastes a private image"` — passes
- `npx vitest run src/AppDocument.test.tsx` — passes (all 13)
- `npm test` — fails (1 of 93)

A test that only fails in company is not trustworthy. It hides real image regressions and it will keep breaking CI at random.

## Failure

```
AssertionError: expect(element).toHaveAttribute("src", "blob:pasted-image-1")
Expected: src="blob:pasted-image-1"
Received: src="blob:pasted-preview"
  at src/AppDocument.test.tsx:338
```

The image is still showing the local preview blob. It has not swapped to the stored image URL.

## Hypothesis (needs confirming)

Line 337 asserts `revokeObjectURL` was called with `blob:pasted-preview`, and that assertion passes. So the revoke happened but the DOM still shows the old `src`.

That points at a race, not a broken feature: the swap from preview blob to stored URL is async, and line 338 uses a synchronous `getByRole`. Under a loaded full-suite run React has not flushed the re-render yet. On its own the machine is fast enough to win the race.

## Work

1. Confirm the race. Change line 338 to an awaited `findByRole` / `waitFor` and rerun `npm test` several times.
2. Decide which side is wrong:
   - If awaiting fixes it, the **test** was wrong. Fix the assertion.
   - If it still fails, the **product** is wrong: the preview URL is revoked before the stored URL is in the DOM, so a reader could see a dead blob image. Fix the swap order in the editor.
3. Rule out cross-file pollution as a second cause (shared blob-URL counter or module state leaking between test files).

## Done when

`npm test` passes 10 runs in a row, and the reason for the original failure is written down — test bug or product bug, not "it went away".

## Notes

Found while fixing the Vercel build failure in `src/lib/instant-document-persistence.ts` (commit 7dde304). This failure is unrelated to that fix — it already failed on `origin/main` at 1ee5895 without it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10: stored Instant URLs no longer replace a pasted preview until the replacement is displayable. Preview blobs stay until unmount or document switch. npm test 96/96.

comments.author: darrenbryant
comments.text:
Diagnosis: product swap-order bug that made the test racy.

Pending preview URLs were spread after stored sources, so save revoked blob:pasted-preview while the img still used it. waitFor then saw blob:pasted-image-1 on the next render. Isolated test also failed here, so this is not cross-file mock or blob-URL counter leakage.

Fix: stored imageSources win the merge so the published URL is in the DOM before revoke. Test waits for that src and records src at revoke time.

npm test passed 10/10 after the fix. typecheck, lint, and production build passed.

title: Copy Share and Edit Links in one gesture
description:
## Outcome

From the Share dialog, an author can copy the read-only Share Link or the private Edit Link in one gesture. They do not have to select truncated mono text, hope the full URL was highlighted, and paste it somewhere to confirm.

Either clicking the link copies it immediately, or a dedicated copy control (icon or button) beside each link does the same thing. There is one control per link type: Share Link and Edit Link.

## Why

The Share dialog currently renders each URL in a truncated `.link-box` span with no copy action. Selecting the visible text is slow and easy to get wrong. The original Split Desk spec already called for a Copy control on the right of each link box; the prototype had Copy buttons with distinct toasts.

## Work

- Add a one-gesture copy action for the read-only Share Link.
- Add a separate one-gesture copy action for the private Edit Link.
- Copy the full absolute URL, not the truncated visible text.
- Confirm the copy with the existing toast pattern. Share and Edit copies must not share one identical message: the Edit copy should remind the author to keep that link private.
- Keep the action keyboard-operable and named for assistive technology.
- Copying must not navigate away, close the dialog, or publish/save.

## Out of scope

- Fixing Share Links that open as unavailable (separate bead)
- Copying the footer status URL, unless the same control is reused there without extra scope
- QR codes, share sheets, mailto, or social sharing
- Changing Edit Link rotation or deletion
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Default to the settled Split Desk link box: sunken field, truncated mono URL, copy control on the right. The prototype used a small "Copy" button; an equivalent copy icon is acceptable if it has a visible accessible name (not hover-only).
- Clicking the truncated URL to copy is also acceptable, including as an extra affordance, but it cannot replace a dedicated named control unless the URL itself is a keyboard-focusable control with an accessible name that says it copies.
- There are two independent actions. Copying the Share Link must never put the Edit Link on the clipboard, and vice versa.
- Use the Clipboard API through a small, testable helper. Do not reach into `document.execCommand` from several UI call sites. If clipboard permission fails, show a recoverable message and leave the dialog open with the full URL still visible and selectable.
- Reuse the existing toast. A copy fired while another toast is visible must still update. Suggested copy: "Share link copied" and "Edit link copied — keep it private" (prototype wording).
- Keep URL construction in the navigation module (`shareUrl` / `editUrl`). The copy action must not invent a second path grammar.
- Do not turn the URLs into ordinary navigation links. Copy is the action; opening the Share Link remains the existing "Open share link" toast path.
- Tests observe: each control copies the correct full URL, keyboard activation works, toasts distinguish Share vs Edit, a clipboard failure does not close the dialog, and truncation in CSS does not change the copied value.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Share dialog offers a one-gesture copy for the read-only Share Link and a separate one-gesture copy for the private Edit Link.
- Activating either action puts that full absolute URL on the clipboard and does not navigate, save, or close the dialog.
- A toast confirms the copy; the Edit Link confirmation tells the author to keep it private.
- Each control is keyboard-operable and has an accessible name that identifies which link it copies.
- Clipboard failure leaves the dialog open with the URLs still visible.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
close_reason: Merged in PR #14 (e6111bd). Share dialog now has named Copy controls for the Share Link and the Edit Link, backed by a single clipboard helper, with distinct toasts and a recoverable failure path.
